# Lucy

## Overview

- **Age:** Seven years old  <sub>[v2 c10 P86](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0086), [v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c8 P5](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolchild  <sub>[v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Lucy is a quiet, neat young girl with long, sleek blond curls and gentle, mild hazel eyes. Her face features a straight nose and a mouth that frequently settles into a prim, restrained expression. She habitually appears immaculate, as though freshly starched and ironed.

_Sources: [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c8 P44](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0044)_

## Personality

Lucy is exceptionally well-behaved, decorous, dependable, and submissive. She absorbs her lessons like a small automaton without complaint and follows instructions with great care. Though naturally gentle, quiet, and easily frightened, she can display quiet composure even during frightening situations like severe storms. However, her extreme rigidity and unvarying perfection make her appear predictable and simple to those around her.

_Sources: [v2 c7 P30](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0030), [v2 c8 P44](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0044), [v2 c10 P14](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0014), [v2 c10 P85](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0085), [v2 c10 P88](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0088), [v2 c10 P89](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0089), [v2 c14 P30](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0030), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c24 P25](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0025), [v2 c26 P33](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0033)_

## History

Following the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Upon their arrival, Lucy immediately distinguished herself through her polite manners and immaculate appearance, though her brother frequently tormented her by pulling her hair, taking her food, or tricking her into dangerous misadventures, such as locking her in a toolhouse or urging her onto a pigpen fence. She began attending local Sunday school, where she memorized hymns and verses submissively, and helped diligently with small tasks around the farm. When school opened, she was enrolled as a pupil under Nell, sitting provisionally alongside Mirabel Cotton, who terrified her with tales of a deceased roaming uncle until Nell intervened. Following her father Richard Farrow's death, a trust fund of two thousand dollars was established for her and Robin, securing their permanent home at Grey Shutters. She subsequently began a neatly kept garden plot and survived a terrifying severe hailstorm by remaining calm and reciting her prayers.

_Sources: [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c8 P6](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0006), [v2 c8 P11](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0011), [v2 c8 P12](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0012), [v2 c8 P17](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0017), [v2 c8 P49](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0049), [v2 c10 P36](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0036), [v2 c14 P30](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0030), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000), [v2 c21 P7](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0007), [v2 c21 P8](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0008), [v2 c22 P22](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0022), [v2 c22 P25](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0025), [v2 c24 P10](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0010), [v2 c24 P25](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0025), [v2 c24 P30](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0030)_

## Quotes

> Robin forced me to balance on the pigpen fence. I refused at first, but he taunted me by calling me a fraid-cat. Then I tumbled down inside the pigpen, which ruined my dress with dirt, and the pig charged straight across me. Even though my dress looked terrible, Robin promised to spray it clean if I stood beneath the pump, so I obeyed him and he drenched me with water, yet my dress remains just as dirty, while my beautiful shoes and sash are completely ruined.  <sub>[v2 c8 P49](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0049)</sub>

> Robin and I came over to see Nutmeg, however we could not see him in the end, though Robin forced him to swear by kicking against the door. And after that Robin took me to this place and rushed away and closed the door; and I was unable to escape. I wept and wept, I was terrified, and oh, I’m so hungry and cold; and I believed you’d never arrive, Nell.  <sub>[v2 c10 P36](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0036)</sub>

> I’m . . . I’m scared. I . . . I don’t wish to ascend to the upper floor by myself in the pitch-black.  <sub>[v2 c21 P3](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0003)</sub>

> Of . . . of Mirabel Cotton’s uncle. In school today, Mirabel Cotton related everything concerning her family to me. Almost all the people in her family are dead . . . every one of her grandfathers and grandmothers, along with a great many uncles and aunts. According to Mirabel, dying is a habit they have. Mirabel feels terribly proud about possessing such a large number of deceased relatives, and she described to me the cause of death for each one, as well as their final words and their appearance inside their coffins. Furthermore, Mirabel states that after his burial, a certain uncle of hers was spotted roaming about the house. Her mother observed him. The others do not bother me quite as much, but I am unable to stop reflecting on that uncle.  <sub>[v2 c21 P7](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0007)</sub>

> Oh, Robin, the asking has to be done by the men.  <sub>[v2 c27 P12](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0012)</sub>
